title: Zesty Egyptian Callaloo Stew
description: A vibrant and pungent stew from Egypt, featuring callaloo and double-fried chicken-style tofu for a vegan-friendly twist. This light and comforting stew is perfect for a sick day.

ingredients.name: double-fried tofu
ingredients.notes: use store-bought or homemade, and cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is translucent, about 8 minutes.
Add the paprika, cumin, salt, and black pepper and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the double-fried tofu and cook for 2-3 minutes, until lightly browned.
Add the callaloo and cook, stirring occasionally, until it has wilted and the flavors have melded together, about 5-7 minutes.

Add the water, lemon juice, and chopped parsley and scallions. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 15-20 minutes, or until the callaloo has broken down and the flavors have thickened.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Serve the stew hot, garnished with additional parsley and scallions if desired.
Refrigerate or freeze leftovers for up to 3 days.
Reheat the stew over low heat, adding a little water if necessary to achieve the desired consistency.
Serve over rice, couscous, or enjoy as a soup.
This stew is best served immediately after cooking, as the flavors will mellow out over time. However, it can be refrigerated or frozen for up to 3 days for a quick and easy meal.
To reheat, simply microwave or reheat in a saucepan over low heat, adding a little water if necessary to achieve the desired consistency.
